question: Xi Jinping out before 2027?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if China's General Secretary of the Communist Party, Xi Jinping, is removed from power for any length of time between July 3, 2025, and December 31, 2026, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

CCP General Secretary Xi Jinping will be considered removed from power if he announces his resignation from his role as General Secretary, or is otherwise dismissed, detained, disqualified, or otherwise loses his position or is prevented from fulfilling his duties as General Secretary within this market's timeframe.

The primary resolution source for this market will be a consensus of credible reporting.

eventMetadata.context_description: Xi Jinping faces no scheduled leadership transition or institutional mechanism for removal before the 21st Party Congress expected in autumn 2027, which falls after the market's December 31, 2026 resolution date. Traders assign overwhelming probability to "No" because Xi has consolidated authority over the Politburo Standing Committee, the Central Military Commission, and party organs, with no designated successor or visible factional challenge capable of forcing an early exit. Recent personnel purges within the People's Liberation Army and the absence of elite defections reinforce this stability. While low-probability events such as a sudden health crisis or unprecedented internal revolt could theoretically alter the outcome, current political structures and elite alignment strongly favor continuity through the end of 2026.

Further separation could emerge from strong midterm results, formal campaign launches, or shifts in voter priorities on economic and foreign policy issues.
